correctness.rationale: Two independent direct orientation-counting arguments derive the closed polynomials. The sole potentially failing log-concavity inequality is at coefficient index two; exact algebra gives both necessary-and-sufficient inequalities. The k=6 reentrant interval factors as (r-3)(r-8), and the all-orientation first k at r=3 follows the exact boundary k<=24(1-2^-k)^2. A translated binomial-plus-linear expression yields the rigorous parity-based complete real-root count. Direct edge-orientation enumeration up to 15 edges and a larger arithmetic grid independently corroborate. No finite enumeration is used to prove an infinite claim.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Published clique bouquets consist of one hub and disjoint cliques and have a universally strictly log-concave acyclic sink polynomial. Complete split graphs with clique size at least two and at least three independent vertices are structurally different; their explicit acyclic coefficient inequality fails for k=6 and 4<=r<=7. The 2019 general recurrence and the 2026 sink-set expansion are starting identities rather than previously stated equivalent two-parameter phase conclusions. Published claw-free root results cannot imply the failures on claw-containing graphs.

value.rationale: Complete split graphs are a canonical chordal family outside the claw-free domain of new sink-root theorems. The sharp two-parameter shape inequalities give meaningful counterexample boundaries; for fixed clique size six the acyclic polynomial loses and later recovers log-concavity even while non-real roots persist. Simultaneous classification of acyclic and unrestricted sink laws is an interpretable structural comparison, not an isolated unexplained finite census.
